referents.why: 'to them' (autois) in 'Pilate was saying to them' is the crowd; not a candidate

referents.why: 'What evil' (ti kakon), interrogative object of 'did He commit': it names no referent
'Him' in 'Crucify Him' is Jesus; the candidates offered (Pilate, Barabbas) do not fit, and Jesus is not offered
referents.category: object not offered as a candidate

referents.why: 'he' (did He commit) is Jesus, the accused; he is not offered as a candidate
referents.category: subject not offered as a candidate

referents.why: the imperative 'crucify' is said to the one who can order it: the crowd cries to Pilate, the questioner; second singular fits Pilate

links.why: 'Pilate was saying: did He commit evil' is speech; the question is its content (R1)
cl0 is the speech verb; cl1 is the question said (R1)
'they shouted: Crucify Him' is speech; the command is its content (R1)
cl2 is the saying (shouted) and cl3 the command said (R1)
'but they shouted all the louder' is a contrast to Pilate's question, not a next event; the Greek has no fused waw
links.category: sequence read where the text says but

links.why: the connective de (but) carried by cl2 sets the shouting against Pilate's questioning in cl0 (mid-verse, backward link)

groups.why: Pilate's question with Pilate as sender; the addressee is removed because the crowd is not a candidate
the shouting crowd is the sender but is not a candidate; the builder's sender w10 is the King of 15.9 and is not offered here; Pilate is the addressee of the command

cant_tell.why: the crowd is not offered as a candidate in this verse
